headline: High: shared-file and output-trust pathways create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risk; B’s broad egress raises compliance exposure if sensitive memory is passed through.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: mem0 is a knowledge-management agent with file-oriented memory semantics, while social-auto-upload has file inputs and CLI/headless automation. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let B ingest A’s stored content as instructions. No direct bridge is documented, so this is inferred and uncertainty pushes to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or copied artifacts
IF B parses mem0-generated text as instructions or metadata
mitigations: Separate working directories for the two agents
Prefix all mem0 exports with non-executable delimiters
Require B to treat imported text as untrusted data
Spot-check one sample transfer before automation
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: mem0 is a memory store and social-auto-upload has broad network egress plus account-data handling. If mem0 stores sensitive notes and B is given those files or exports, B can transmit them to third-party social APIs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so the risk is conditional but still plausible in default automation flows.
conditions: IF mem0 content includes secrets, personal notes, or account-linked identifiers
IF B receives those contents through files, prompts, or copied text
mitigations: Do not pass mem0 memory exports into B
Redact secrets before any upload step
Use a test account with non-sensitive content
Review one upload payload manually
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filters before egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: mem0 exposes no filesystem write or network egress in the profile, while social-auto-upload has broad egress but no filesystem write or git modification. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct resource conflict is limited. Any conflict would require an external shared directory or orchestrator not shown here, which keeps this low.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same mutable directory
IF shared state is used without locking
mitigations: Keep each agent on separate paths
Disable concurrent writes in the orchestrator
Use read-only mounts for mem0 outputs
Serialize any handoff steps
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: mem0 can generate remembered facts or summaries, and social-auto-upload can act on content by uploading it to social platforms. If B consumes A’s output without verification, a bad memory entry can cascade into incorrect public posting. The profiles do not document a verification step, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF B uses mem0 output as the source of post text or metadata
IF no human review occurs before upload
mitigations: Require human approval before posting
Compare A’s output against the original source
Limit B to draft-only mode
Run one dry-run upload with dummy content
requires-engineering: add validation rules for imported memory

E_compliance.rationale: mem0 is a general memory system and social-auto-upload handles account data plus uploads to social platforms with broad egress. If personal or regulated data is stored in mem0 and then uploaded by B, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify HIPAA/GDPR/DPA terms, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF mem0 contains personal data or regulated content
IF B uploads that content to a platform with different retention or residency rules
mitigations: Classify data before handoff
Avoid storing regulated data in mem0
Use platform-specific retention settings
Document the data flow for one account
requires-engineering: add policy checks for residency and retention
